chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Abu Dawud from some of our companions from Muhammad ibn Marwan said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I pass by fruit (on the tree) and eat from it.' He said, 'Eat, but do not carry (take away).' I said, 'May I be your ransom, indeed the merchants have bought it and paid their money.' He said, 'They bought what is not theirs.'

key_terms.الثَّمَرَة: Fruit (specifically fruit still on the tree)
key_terms.تَحْمِلْ: To carry/take away (implies removing from the tree/ground)
key_terms.مَا لَيْسَ لَهُمْ: What is not theirs (indicating lack of full ownership/possession)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating fruit from a tree and the conditions for merchants' ownership of unharvested fruit?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of *Bay' al-Thamar* (sale of fruit), distinguishing between mere consumption and legal possession. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that merchants who paid for fruit still attached to the tree have purchased 'what is not yet theirs,' highlighting the condition of separation (*Tanazzul*) for ownership transfer. This underscores the importance of risk and actual possession in commercial transactions, a key topic in Usul al-Fiqh debates regarding conditional sales.
